newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says Treasury agrees tax upped by Tories.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says Treasury agrees tax upped by Tories.

text.p: The opposition Labour party said on Thursday that official Treasury figures disproved ruling party statements that tax had come down under the Conservatives.

Labour's Shadow Chief Secretary to the Treasury, Alistair Darling, told a news conference that the figures, released in a written reply to a parliamentary question, showed the share of both direct and indirect tax had risen since the 1992 election.
The tax burden on a family with two children and one average income had risen from 32.7 percent in 1992/3 to 35.11 percent in 1997/8, Darling said.
The share of direct tax had risen from 20.2 percent to 20.71 percent, while the share of indirect tax had risen from 12.5 percent to 14.4 percent in the same period, he said.
"What they (the Conservatives) have said is simply not true...the burden of tax has gone up," he said.
Prime Minister John Major is currently featuring in a Conservative election campaign poster saying the government had delivered lower taxes as promised.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke cut one percentage point off taxes in the last budget, but Labour argues this fails to make up for a string of direct and indirect tax rises introduced by the ruling party since 1992.
Taxes were the main battleground of the 1992 election, with Labour hurt badly by a Conservative advertising campaign focussing on "Labour's tax bombshell".

But Darling said Labour had no plans to report the Conservatives to the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) over the current campaign. "I'm not sure the ASA is the best court. The best court is the people of this country," he said.
Darling said the written answer had been due the day after the November budget but had been delayed for reasons not explained to him.
"The fact that this has been delayed confirms my suspicions that the Conservatives have something to hide," he said. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
